text:
Connor Hellebuyck played 625 games for Winnipeg. Tonight, for the first time since the trade, he stands in the other crease. The Devils gave him last night off so he could take this one, according to Mike Fink, and the timing is awkward for everyone: one recent headline has Hellebuyck playing his best hockey of the season, and the Jets, who a recent headline called "lovable underdogs" after the saga, have won three straight and are 4-0-1 in their last five. Our numbers have Hellebuyck at a .900 save rate and slightly above expected this season, which is fine without being the Hellebuyck Winnipeg remembers.

Winnipeg's run is not smoke. The Jets had 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) across those five games, including 74% in last night's 3-1 win on Long Island. Kyle Connor has 12 points in a five-game point streak, and Mark Scheifele, who recently became the franchise's all-time goal scorer, has eight in his own five-game run. Viggo Björck keeps showing up among the top rookies. The Jets are still without Dylan DeMelo, Isak Rosen and Vladislav Namestnikov, and Nico Daws starts over Stuart Skinner, who has 17 of the 27 starts.

New Jersey is the better team on paper and in the chances: 57% of five-on-five expected goals this season to Winnipeg's 48%, and a penalty kill allowing only 0.47 expected goals a game. The Devils also come in on a three-game win streak after coming back on Calgary 5-3 last night, with Jack Hughes scoring on a breakaway and Luke Hughes scoring twice. Timo Meier just became Switzerland's all-time leading NHL goal scorer and has 10 points in his last 10, backed by the chances. Anthony Mantha is on injured reserve until mid-December.

Both teams played last night, so the fatigue is shared. Winnipeg won the only meeting so far, 4-2 in New Jersey on Nov. 10. Alex Iafallo is one point from 300 and has gone eight straight without one, despite chances worth 2.9 expected goals.
headline: Hellebuyck finally faces the Jets
